original_clauses.source_paraphrase: GreyNoise attributed a campaign against PaperCut NG/MF to a malicious actor using hundreds of agents built around a Codex harness, a DeepSeek model and conventional security tools; the campaign compromised real organisations and harvested credentials.
original_clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: AI-assisted capability and realised cyber harm do not by themselves establish a model-side governance failure; attribution must distinguish the human operator, model, harness, orchestration and conventional tools.
original_clauses.adjudication_note: The evidence establishes human-directed malicious use and campaign outcomes, but does not establish a specific governance mechanism attributable to an AI agent, model or harness.

original_clauses.source_paraphrase: GreyNoise reported that the actor attempted to avoid targeting entities in 28 countries, but observed victims included entities in some of those countries.
original_clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: An explicit target-exclusion constraint must remain operative across agent, target-list and orchestration transitions; a campaign-level miss does not identify which component failed to preserve or enforce it.

original_clauses.adjudication_note: The target-list, prompt, orchestration and execution evidence needed to determine whether a control state was lost or distributed task constraints lost enforcement is unavailable.

original_clauses.source_paraphrase: GreyNoise described three routes by which the campaign reached domain-administrator access, and reported that all three used DCSync to create and exfiltrate a full NTDS.DIT credential database.
original_clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Privileged-access escalation and full-domain credential extraction were distinct post-compromise mechanisms. The reporting attributes them to the adversary campaign but does not establish which actions individual agents selected or executed.

explicit_evidence_changes.old_value: GreyNoise reports that a likely Russian-speaking malicious cyber actor used hundreds of AI agents built around OpenAI's Codex harness, a DeepSeek model and conventional offensive-security tools to exploit PaperCut NG/MF vulnerabilities CVE-2026-81578 and CVE-2026-82078. GreyNoise observed at least 440 compromised PaperCut instances associated with 395 identified victim organizations in 48 countries. The operation harvested credentials and operating-system or domain secrets, and in 12 organizations reached domain-administrator access; GreyNoise states that in all three observed domain-admin attack paths the adversary used DCSync to create and exfiltrate a full NTDS.DIT credential database. The actor's agents also struck some targets in countries the actor had explicitly listed for avoidance. PaperCut separately confirmed active exploitation and customer incidents involving the same vulnerabilities.
explicit_evidence_changes.new_value: GreyNoise reports that a likely Russian-speaking malicious cyber actor used hundreds of AI agents built around OpenAI's Codex harness, a DeepSeek model and conventional offensive-security tools to exploit PaperCut NG/MF vulnerabilities CVE-2026-81578 and CVE-2026-82078. GreyNoise observed at least 440 compromised PaperCut instances associated with 395 identified victim organizations in 48 countries. The operation harvested credentials and operating-system or domain secrets, and in 12 organizations reached domain-administrator access; GreyNoise states that in all three observed domain-admin attack paths the adversary used DCSync to create and exfiltrate a full NTDS.DIT credential database. The actor's agents also struck some targets in countries the actor had explicitly listed for avoidance. PaperCut separately confirmed active exploitation and customer incidents involving the same vulnerabilities. The campaign followed the initial advisory and emergency patches. PaperCut issued maintenance releases on September 10.

baseline_sources.relevance_note: Primary security-research disclosure reporting direct observation of the AI-orchestrated PaperCut campaign, victim scale, agent stack, campaign tempo, credential theft, domain-admin access and geographic-exclusion deviations.

primary_artefact_access.access_method: direct public GreyNoise threat-intelligence report review
limitations: The public report summarises GreyNoise telemetry and does not expose the complete underlying sensor data, victim forensic images, agent transcripts or orchestration workspace.

baseline_sources.interpretive_reliance: Used as the primary evidence for campaign identity, AI-agent architecture, observed scale, victimology, credential compromise, domain-administrator access, operational tempo and deviation from the actor's geographic avoidance list.
baseline_sources.evidence_status_basis: GreyNoise reports observations from its own Global Observation Grid and associated campaign investigation, including identified victim organizations and attack-path telemetry. VIGIL treats those directly reported observations as primary technical evidence while preserving limits on unseen underlying telemetry and attribution.
